dimensions.label: What the entry plan includes
dimensions.a: Unlimited users and unlimited contacts on every plan, including the $97 Starter
dimensions.b: The $97 Launch plan caps out at 2 team-member seats and 10,000 contacts

dimensions.label: How the bill grows with usage
dimensions.a: The plan price never changes; texts, calls, email and most AI draw from a prepaid wallet that recharges itself automatically
dimensions.b: No usage meter inside your contact and email-send limits; going over the cap on Launch means upgrading to Scale at $197 or higher

dimensions.label: Calling, texting and phone numbers
dimensions.a: Local and toll-free numbers, calls and SMS are built in on every plan, billed per use from the wallet
dimensions.b: No built-in phone numbers, calls or SMS sending

dimensions.label: Email sending limits
dimensions.a: Metered per email sent, with no monthly send cap on any plan
dimensions.b: A monthly send allowance by plan, from 50,000 on Launch up to 1,200,000 on Dominate

dimensions.label: Percentage taken from each sale
dimensions.a: Not part of HighLevel's pricing model; no percent-of-sales fee is published on its pricing page
dimensions.b: None; ClickFunnels' pricing-page FAQ states it takes no percentage of sales

dimensions.label: Online courses and community
dimensions.a: Courses and communities are included, but positioned as a secondary feature next to the CRM and phone system
dimensions.b: 3 courses on Launch, rising to 20 on Dominate, with community included on every tier

dimensions.label: Running multiple client accounts
dimensions.a: Starter includes 3 sub-accounts; Unlimited ($297) and Agency Pro ($497) remove that cap and allow rebilling phone and email usage to clients
dimensions.b: Workspaces scale from 1 on Launch to 20 on Dominate; ClickFunnels publishes no client-rebilling or SaaS-resale feature

dimensions.label: Contract and billing flexibility
dimensions.a: Month-to-month on every plan; annual billing costs exactly 10 months' price
dimensions.b: Launch, Scale and Optimize can be billed monthly or annually; Dominate is sold annually only, at $5,997 a year

dimensions.label: Refunds and cancellation
dimensions.a: HighLevel's terms call all fees non-refundable, and a canceled account's data is deleted after 90 days
dimensions.b: A 30-day money-back guarantee applies, and plans can be changed at any time

dimensions.label: Free trial clarity
dimensions.a: A 14-day free trial is stated on the pricing page; whether a card is required upfront was not confirmed
dimensions.b: A trial button exists, but its length and card requirement are not stated on the current pricing or signup pages

verdicts.why: An agency managing several client accounts gets sub-accounts, unlimited seats and at-cost or marked-up rebilling built for that job; ClickFunnels' workspaces are not paired with a rebilling or SaaS-resale feature.
ClickFunnels bundles courses, community and funnels into every tier; a course creator gets that without paying for a phone system and CRM they are unlikely to use.

Neither tool is a storefront platform; a Shopify-store owner already has checkout covered and should judge GoHighLevel or ClickFunnels only as an add-on for CRM, email or funnels, not as the store itself.
A clinic, contractor or salon runs on booking, reviews and follow-up texts, which GoHighLevel bundles with its CRM; ClickFunnels has no built-in calling, texting or booking calendar.
A freelancer selling one offer needs a funnel and checkout, not a phone system and client sub-accounts; ClickFunnels' $97 Launch plan covers that without GoHighLevel's usage-metered wallet.

Neither platform is built for subscription-software sales; a SaaS startup needs product-led signup and billing tools that GoHighLevel's phone-first CRM and ClickFunnels' funnel-and-course platform were not designed to provide.
